dedupe_keys.name: iberian peninsula blackout of 28 april 2025 excess mortality in spain and portugal

description: This study estimates how many deaths the power outage of 28 April 2025 caused across mainland Spain and Portugal, where the grid was down for about ten hours and eight deaths were reported directly. Garyfallos Konstantinoudis of the Grantham Institute at Imperial College London and Julien Riou posted it on medRxiv in June 2025, and the preprint server links a later version in Nature Communications. Bayesian models that account for temperature, holidays and spatiotemporal trends give expected deaths for the blackout week, which are compared with observed deaths by age, sex and region. Excess deaths were limited on the day itself, but in Spain mortality rose over the next two days by about 167 deaths, with a 95 percent credible interval of 28 to 300, particularly among women aged 85 and over; no clear excess appeared in Portugal. Coverage is the two countries by region. Format and access: preprint and journal article. Licence: preprint CC-BY-NC-4.0; the Nature Communications article is CC-BY-4.0 (read on 2026-09-29); free. Caveats: attribution to the blackout rests on modelled baselines, and only the rights section of the journal version was read. It quantifies health impacts of grid failure for resilience and emergency response planning. A related catalogue record is the Puerto Rico Hurricane Maria restoration assessment.
